newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE to meet in special session on Serbia polls.
newsitem.headline: OSCE to meet in special session on Serbia polls.

text.p: Europe's security forum was scheduled to meet in special session on Friday to discuss a report on disputed municipal elections in Serbia drawn up last week by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez.
The permanent council of the Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) was due to convene at 3 p.m. local time (1400 GMT), an OSCE spokeswoman said.

"The permanent council has been called into special session today and will be focusing on the report by Mr Gonzalez and the situation in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
The OSCE's decision-making permanent council, and Denmark, which took over the OSCE presidency on January 1, are awaiting a response from Belgrade to Gonzalez's report.

Gonzalez issued a report on December 27 on his on-the-spot investigations into municipal elections on November 17, urging Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to respect opposition victories in the polls.
Gonzalez concluded in his OSCE report that the anti-Milosevic Zajedno coalition had fairly won the local elections in 13 key provincial centres as well as in nine municipalities in Belgrade.
Thousands of demonstrators have poured on to the streets in the past 46 days to protest the annulment of the opposition victories amid growing international criticism of Milosevic.

Milosevic invited the OSCE to send a team to investigate the election dispute, but it was not immediately clear what action the 54-member body can take against Yugoslavia if it ignores Gonzalez's recommendations.
The forum suspended Yugoslavia, now consisting of Serbia and Montenegro, in 1992 accusing Belgrade of helping to stoke the war in neighbouring Bosnia.
